reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown read Numbers 15 as an omission and Leviticus 4 as a positive transgression, so the differing offerings answer two distinct sins.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "What must a congregation do if it sins through ignorance?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/congregation.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
sides.verseText: when the sin in which they have sinned is known, then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.

sides.snippet: one young bull for a burnt offering…and one male goat for a sin-offering.
sides.verseText: then it shall be, if it be done unwittingly, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bull for a burnt offering, for a sweet savor to Yahweh, with the meal-offering of it, and the drink-offering of it, according to the ordinance, and one male goat for a sin-offering.
